To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthetic mitoNEET cluster model 52- is structurally similar to its biological counterpart and that the unique {SN} ligand of this cluster mediates proton coupled electron transfer.

a synthetic analogue of mitoNEET with biomimetic ligation of the [2Fe- 2S] cluster was structurally characterized and shown to mediate PCET at its unique His ligand site, pointing at the potential functional role of this ligand in the enzyme.
a biomimetic [2Fe- 2S] cluster model for MitoNEET was structurally characterized and found to be able to mediate PCET at the {SN}-ligated site.

the development of a biomimetic {NS/S2} capped [2F-2S] model complex of the mitoNEEt protein and the investigation of its reactivity towards a variety of redox active substrates.
the development of a biomimetic model for the [2Fe- 2S] cluster in mitoNEET and with the investigation of its PCET properties.
the synthesis and structural characterization of a synthetic analogue of the mitoNEEt [2Fe- 2S] cluster.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mitoNEEt model complex is a very good structural mimic for the natural cofactor, but its reactivity is not a good mimic for the biological system.
the mitoNEet model 5H2 reacts with a similar thermodynamics, but with a significantly lower rate than 4H2.
mitoNEET is a proton-coupled electron transfer protein, but that this function is not directly related to its [2Fe- 2S] cluster, as it is the case for other [2Fe-4S] cluster proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitoNEet model is a very good model of the biological cofactor in terms of structural integrity, but that its PCET reactivity is not as efficient as for the homolepic model.
mitoNEET is able to catalyze PCET reactions at the {SN/S2}-ligated Fe site, and that the His ligand is crucial in this process.
the mitoNEet [2Fe- 2S] cluster is a good candidate for a proton coupled electron transfer catalyst.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mitoNEet model complex 52- is not only a structural model but also a functional model for the enzyme's [2Fe- 2S] cluster, and that the enzyme may mediate PCET at its {SN} ligating histidine residue.
mitoNEET may be able to control the rate of PCET reactions at the {SN/S2/S2/S2} site by adjusting its pKa.

the mitoNEEt model 52- is a high fidelity structural and functional model of the biological [2Fe-4S] cofactor, and it is the first model to show proton coupled electron transfer at the {SN}-coordinated site.
